articles.text: It will be noticed by our market report, that cattle are from five to twenty cents higher on all classes, than last week.
articles.summary: Cattle prices are up five to twenty cents on all classes from the previous week.

articles.text: The immigration this year to Dakota bids fair to rival that of two years ago. The N. P. is making extremely low rates to all intending settlers.
articles.summary: Dakota immigration expected to rival 1883's, helped by low Northern Pacific rates.

articles.text: All the U. S. treasury money has been counted and the amount found correct to a cent. So much for Republican corruption. The Democrats can well be proud to show such a record.
articles.summary: Comment on the treasury count finding all funds correct.

articles.text: The Illinois senatorial contest is coming to a focus. Morrison's name will be dropped by the Democrats if he cannot secure a full vote and some other name proposed. The Republicans are still loyal to Logan and have the best chances of success.
articles.summary: Comment on the Illinois U.S. Senate contest between Morrison and Logan.

articles.text: There has been fighting at Batoche, between Gen. Middleton and Riel's forces, the half-breeds getting rather the best of it. At any rate the dominion troops could not dislodge the enemy and Middleton has sent for more forces. Although the matter must end in Riel's defeat, we can hope that the Dominion will be taught the lesson that it cannot trample on the rights of citizens with impunity.
articles.summary: Comment on the fighting at Batoche in the Riel rebellion.

articles.text: There have been stirring times in England lately, owing to the government's war policy. Gladstone recently was was voted a large credit, supposably with the intention of prosecuting war measures against Russia. As soon as he had this credit, measures were immediately taken to grant Russia everything she demanded and England was thus forced into a very humiliating situation. The war party, lead by Sir Stafford Northcote, has aroused intense feeling against Gladstone and it may end in his overthrow. Should this occur war will likely be declared.
articles.summary: Comment on Gladstone's war credit and the Anglo-Russian crisis.

articles.text: The Deadwood Pioneer, in an article headed "What Arguments," attempts to answer our statements relative to a railroad being built from Medora to the Hills. As our readers will remember our article stated that a large number of the Hills merchants contracted to ship their freight and express via the Northern Pacific to the Hills. These contracts, with a low estimate of the amount of freight and express involved were handed to capitalists who agreed to build the road provided the estimate held good. We know that the actual amount shipped would have been twice as much as the estimate had the Hills merchants stuck to their bargains and in reality the the amount shipped was not half the amount of the estimate. The capitalists could only judge by the facts and as there was not enough business to guarantee a road, refused to build without additional income. These are the facts as we stated them and we might add that the stage line was merely a feeler as to the Hills trade. The Pioneer then talks about the folly of whipping the Hills people into subjection or suffering the vengeance of the Northern Pacific. There was no attempt to whip the Hills people into subjection. They voluntarily signed contracts to ship via the N. P. and as voluntarily broke their promises. No attempt was made to compel them to stick to their agreement and none will be made. As far as the Hills people suffering the vengeance of the N. P. is concerned we will state that the N. P. would have had nothing whatever to do with the road, except that it would get a haul out of the Hills freight. Outside capital entirely was interested in the matter. The Pioneer then states that other roads are building Hillwards, while the N. P. is dozing and grumbling over broken promises. As we have just stated, the N. P. has nothing to do with the contemplated road and the Pioneer should be in far higher business than blaming a corporation for refusing to deal with persons who have violated contracts and then itself finds no word of fault with the contracts breakers. The Pioneer can readily see, that it has in no way answered our article and we will reiterate our former statement that had half the Hills merchants stuck to their promises they would now have direct or convenient railroad connection with the N. P.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy rebuts the Deadwood Pioneer over why a Medora-to-Black Hills railroad was not built, blaming Hills merchants who broke shipping contracts.

articles.headline: Additional Local.
articles.text: A glee club is one of the near probabilities.
articles.summary: A glee club may soon be formed.

articles.text: Miss Maggie Guardient intends going home for a short visit soon.
articles.summary: Miss Maggie Guardient plans a short visit home.

articles.text: Judge [illegible], wife and two daughters are here visiting the Marquis.

articles.summary: Soap works and a tannery are expected to be built in Medora this summer.

articles.text: There is a good prospect of Medora's soon become a money-order office. This will be a great advantage.
articles.summary: Medora may soon become a money-order post office.

articles.text: The saloon-keepers are now sending enough money to Mandan to keep a good school running the year round.
articles.summary: Saloon license money from Medora is going to Mandan.

articles.text: A telegram from J. S. Warn says that he will be home next week "dead or alive," "on the dead square."
articles.summary: J. S. Warn telegraphs that he will be home next week.

articles.text: A. M. Sinnott went east on No. 2, yesterday on his pay to Bismarck. Thence he will go to Marshfield, Mass.
articles.summary: A. M. Sinnott left east for Bismarck and Marshfield, Mass.

articles.text: The survey of the town-plat is completed and Mr. Heinze returned to Bismarck, Monday. It was found that the previous survey was from six inches to four feet out of the way.
articles.summary: The Medora town-plat survey is finished; the earlier survey was found off by up to four feet.

articles.text: John Goodall and Mose Ryder are now pulling all the stock off the stage road and are expected in in a few days.
articles.summary: Goodall and Ryder are pulling all the stock off the stage road.

articles.text: On next Saturday evening at the rink, a prize will be given to the gentleman wearing the largest necktie. Also to the lady wearing the prettiest sun-bonnet.
articles.summary: Prizes planned at the rink Saturday for largest necktie and prettiest sun-bonnet.

articles.text: Dr. Heber Robarts came up last night to look after some of his patients here. He has been retained as family and company physician by the Marquis and will spend about three days a week in Medora, beginning about the first of June.
articles.summary: Dr. Heber Robarts has been retained by the Marquis de Morès as family and company physician.

articles.text: The mile race at the rink last Saturday evening, was won by George Bicknell. In a sbsequent scrub race Johnny Chute beat the first time by over a minute making a mile in six minutes. As there were thirty-six laps to a mile this was fair time.
articles.summary: George Bicknell won the mile race at the rink; Johnny Chute then ran a mile in six minutes.

articles.text: Last year's school committee is having a parrot and monkey time collecting money for school debts. The people in town are kicking at bearing the whole burden and that the license money cannot be used for that purpose, while nothing will be done by the cattle men except as a body.
articles.summary: Last year's school committee is struggling to collect money for school debts.

articles.text: By earnest attention to business and the desire to cater to the wants of all his customers, Chas. Cook has built up a trade that he may well take pride in. He has a full line of stationer's and news goods as well as all kinds of smokers' articles and is constantly improving his stock. Those desiring anything in his line only need a trial to become regular customers.
articles.summary: Praise for Chas. Cook's stationery, news and smokers' goods trade.

articles.text: The Refrigerator Car Co. have nearly completed arrangements to handle cattle for the slaughter-house. The bottoms up the river from Pete Book's coal mine are being entirely cleared of trees and underbrush. The cattle from the Hashknife and the whole southern country will be driven down Sully creek from the divide and those from Montana will come down Garner creek. Two large corrals have been built on the bottom this side of the Custer Trail ranch. They are without doubt the best corrals in this part of the country, being made on the stockade plan and are capable of holding about a thousand cattle each. The animals will be driven into one corral in the evening and in the morning will be weighed on scales 40x14 connecting the two corrals. Thence they will be driven down the river to the slaughter-house. Inside of two years all the bottoms will be plowed and sowed to alfalfa or millet, the object being to get sufficient feed to keep cattle fit for slaughtering at all seasons of the year.
articles.summary: The Refrigerator Car Co. has built two stockade corrals with scales near the Custer Trail ranch and is clearing the river bottoms to supply the slaughter-house.

articles.headline: Annoncement.
articles.text:
Cattle-men of the Little Missouri river are advised that the Northern Pacific Refrigerator Car Company, will give them during June for the beef and dry cows that they wish to sell, Chicago prices less seventy cents per hundred to cover freight and shrinkage. The cattle to be delivered in the evening at the Sully Creek corrals and weighed in the morning.

Marquis de Mores,
President.
articles.summary: The Marquis de Morès announces the N. P. Refrigerator Car Co. will buy beef and dry cows in June at Chicago prices less seventy cents per hundred.

articles.text: The two eastern round-ups, north and south of the track, have finished their work. Very few cattle were found although the round-up went east of Gladstone.
articles.summary: The two eastern round-ups have finished, finding very few cattle.

articles.text: A bill of considerable interest to all stockgrowers in the northwest has been passed by the Illinois legislature. It is a measure to regulate the charges of the Chicago stock yards for yardage, freight grain, hay and other articles furnished and to prevent extortion and unjust discrimination. It provides among other things that the stockyards shall not receive for yardage more than fifteen cents per head for horses, cattle and mules, five cents for hogs and four cents for sheep, nor more than five per cent additional to the current market wholesale price for hay, corn or other articles supplied by them for the sustenance of such animals; and that sales shall be made by actual weight. The penalty for collecting higher rates or unjust discrimination is a fine not less than $300 for the first offense, and not less than $500 nor more than $1,000 for subsequent offense.—[Livingston Enterprise.
articles.summary: Illinois passes a law regulating Chicago stock-yard charges (from the Livingston Enterprise).

articles.text: In answer to several inquiries from the east, we will state that it is very seldom any cattle are fed in this country. The bulk of the cattle have nothing and need nothing to eat but the range grasses. Only in exceptional cases where an animal is very weak and the weather severe is any feeding done. There is enough alkali in the water and grass to furnish cattle all the saline matter they need. Old range cattle almost invariably refuse to touch salt in its crystalline state.
articles.summary: Range cattle are seldom fed and get enough salt from alkali water and grass.

articles.text: A train load of cattle, nine hundred and fifty head, have been quarantined for several days at Sentinel Butte. They belong to F. W. Fry, of Arkansas. It is impossible to learn the cause of the quarantine but it must be on account of Montana's pleuro-pneumonia quarantine law. The owner maintains that the cattle are free from disease although they are very poor. The whole herd was turned loose at the Butte, orders coming from the railroad officials to that effect. There were no horses and only the men on the train to aid in holding the cattle. They are now widely scattered. In whatever light this affair is viewed it is a badly botched mess. If the cattle are free from disease, as the owner claims, and come from a healthy country, it is a great imposition on him. The railroad company had no right to ship the cattle in the first place if they were diseased and by their being scattered at Sentinel Butte endanger other herds. There seems to be no fear of contagion and we are forced into the belief that the owner has been treated unjustly.
articles.summary: A trainload of 950 Arkansas cattle owned by F. W. Fry was quarantined and turned loose at Sentinel Butte.

articles.summary: John Munro is farming the butte farm.

articles.summary: The Frank Keeler family arrived and are boarding at the Pyramid Park hotel.

articles.text: The people have taken hold of "cleaning up" with a will, and now we think we can boast as clean a town as there is on the line of the road.
articles.summary: Medora residents have cleaned up the town.

articles.text: The cold-storage room in the old slaughter-house has been entirely torn out and will be rebuilt on the plan of of those in the new house.
articles.summary: The old slaughter-house cold-storage room is being rebuilt.

articles.text: Any further shooting on this side of the track will mean business or that some would-be bad man is seeking an opportunity to get his head swelled.
articles.summary: A warning against further shooting on the east side of the track.

articles.text: The hotel will be all finished, furnished and ready for business by June 1. Arch. Boyd, the proprietor, has his furniture all bought and will start in good shape.
articles.summary: Arch. Boyd's hotel will open by June 1.

articles.text: A boiler has been set in position in the old slaughter-house to be used in drying blood. What has heretofore been wasted will now net about $20 a ton.
articles.summary: A boiler for drying blood has been installed at the old slaughter-house.

articles.text: A large tank made of boiler plates has been sunk in the well at the slaughter-house. This will sink below the quicksand and make room for an abundance of water.
articles.summary: A boiler-plate tank was sunk in the slaughter-house well.

articles.text: E. G. Paddock has bought Geo. Fitzgerald's old dwelling on the other side of the river and set it up next his barn on this side. Fred Banan will occupy it as a barber shop.
articles.summary: E. G. Paddock moved Geo. Fitzgerald's old house across the river; Fred Banan will use it as a barber shop.

articles.text: Work at the slaughter-house will probably open for the season during the first week in June. Contracts have been signed by which cattle must be delivered here by that time.
articles.summary: The slaughter-house will probably open for the season the first week of June.

articles.text: The side-tracks have all been raised to overcome the grade in getting on the main track. The work under the superintendence of Paul Moore, has been pushed as he only can do it.
articles.summary: The Medora side-tracks were raised under Paul Moore.

articles.text: Superintendent Allen went out on the coach Sunday for the Hills. Should he not return he can be sure of having left behind many friends made during his connection with the stage line.
articles.summary: Stage-line superintendent Allen left for the Black Hills on Sunday's coach.

articles.text: Work will soon begin on turning the railroad right of way into a park. Room will then be left for a wide street and the Co. will erect buildings facing the road. This will wonderfully improve the appearance of Medora from the railroad.

articles.text: On account of Medora's brief existence there are still left evidences of its previous condition in the sage brush, growing on the side lots and streets. It is the intention of the Co. to thoroughly clean up every where to correspond with the good moves made in that direction by the rest of the citizens.
articles.summary: The Company intends to clear sage brush from Medora's lots and streets.

articles.text: Peter Book commenced making brick Monday and will make over a million this summer. The six hundred thousand he made last year have long since been used up and there is immediate need of at least a hundred thousand more. The building to be done this summer will take the remainder of the million.

articles.text: It has been stated as an axiom that a man's business ability can be judged by his advertising. According to this rule, the new clothing store managed by T. W. Gordon, is conducted on first-class principles, as evinced by the large advertisement in this issue. The store is sure to do a large business.
articles.summary: Notice of T. W. Gordon's new clothing store.

articles.text: Especially in the west, there is nothing that improves the appearance of a city more than shade trees. We are glad to see that a number are being set out and more will be soon. The cost is almost nothing and the trouble is slight. There is no reason why shade trees should not adorn the front of every lot in Medora.
articles.summary: Shade trees are being set out in Medora.

articles.text: Hereafter, Mr. Martin's weather report will be published weekly and the summary, as usual, given monthly. Among others, Mr. Rich of the Badger cattle Co., requested this change and Mr. Martin readily agreed. Mr. Rich has been making estimates of the condition of the cattle in relation to weather which may prove of value.

articles.text: In the light of the two fatal accidents happening lately from gun-shot wounds, we again wish to remark that such accidents are little short of criminal. In handling a gun, one always can and should know, not think, that it is loaded or unloaded and govern one's self accordingly. Both are sad lessons to draw a moral from and we hope in the future that we will not again be obliged to chronicle any more such painful accidents.
articles.summary: Editorial on two recent fatal gun accidents.

articles.summary: F. D. Foster is expected back next week with his family.

articles.text: Mrs. Draper is still very ill, although the operation for the removal of a tumor, performed by Drs. Robarts and McIntosh seems to have benefitted her.
articles.summary: Mrs. Draper remains very ill after a tumor operation by Drs. Robarts and McIntosh.

articles.text: Following close on the heels of the news of the accident to Frank Wadsworth, which happened a week ago Tuesday, came the sad news of his death, occuring Friday at noon. It is seldom that a death is so widely mourned as was this one. Frank was a very quiet, unobtrusive man, one who always attended strictly to his business and left the impression of having a reserve force of character that impelled him to do right at all times. It will be remembered that he was accidentally shot last Tuesday and that his leg was amputated Wednesday. He was a splendid patient, cheerfully enduring the agony incident to the operation. Even within a few minutes of his death he was talking pleasantly to the watchers. The bullet was probed for to a depth of eight inches but it could not be found. It undoubtedly entered his abdomen, thus making the fatal wound. The funeral services took place at Belfield last Sunday, a number of citizens from here, attending. Rev. H. B. Shaffner conducted the ceremonies and the body was laid to rest near the church, a beautiful site for the resting place of the dead.
articles.summary: Frank Wadsworth, accidentally shot on a Tuesday, died the following Friday and was buried at Belfield.

articles.headline: Citizens' Meeting.
articles.text:
The meeting last Friday evening was called to order by Marquis de Mores and A. T. Packard was elected chairman.

The chairman stated the objects of the meeting to be, to organize a fire department, to adopt measures to keep the town free of all rubbish, to perfect a school organization and to appoint a committee to see that order is kept.

In reference to the fire department the chairman of the old committee, J. C. Fisher, reported that a sum of money, probably sufficient for present need, had been subscribed but that no word had as yet been received from F. D. Foster relative to material. Further time was given the committee. Chief of the fire department were then elected as follows: J. A. Ferris and J. B. Walker on the west side of the river and A. T. Packard and Bob. Roberts on the east side.

A report of the old school board by J. C. Fisher was then given by which it appeared that about $40.00 was yet due on last term's expenses. Sufficient money had been guaranteed, however, and the old board was requested to collect the amount due and liquidate all indebtedness. It was decided to begin a new term of school as soon as practicable, a new board being appointed, consisting of H. M. Jorgens, Wm. Van Driesche and J. A. Ferris.

The cleanliness of the town was then considered and a committee consisting of J. C. Fisher, Wm. Van Driesche and C. F. Brown, was appointed to request all citizens to thoroughly clean their premises and to keep them clean.

As there is no county organization here means were discussed to preserve good order and it was decided that the fire committee, Messrs. Packard & Robberts should give their personal attention to the subject of good order.

No more business coming before the meeting, it was declared adjourned.
articles.summary: A citizens' meeting called by the Marquis de Morès and chaired by A. T. Packard organized fire chiefs, a new school board, a cleanliness committee and arrangements for keeping order.

Freighters Attention! — King jeweler, Spearfish or Deadwood, watch repairs
Frank Frisby, Drugs, Paints and Oils, Bismarck, Dak. — correspondence solicited
Cedar Posts for Sale — good cedar posts delivered in Medora and on the cars, $15 per hundred; G. D. Kennedy, Medora, Dak.
General Store of the N. P. R. C. Co., Medora, Dakota — groceries, dry goods, ready-made clothing, hats, caps, canned goods, harness, saddles, tobacco and cigars, felt shoes, overshoes, boots and shoes, flour and feed; hunters outfits a specialty; wholesale and retail
Northern Pacific Railroad — the direct line between St. Paul, Minneapolis or Duluth and the Pacific Northwest; Pullman sleepers, dining cars, free emigrant sleepers, the only all-rail line to Yellowstone National Park; Chas. S. Fee, General Passenger Agent, St. Paul
City Drug Store, Medora, Dak., H. M. Jorgens, Proprietor — drugs, patent medicines, perfumery, toilet articles, notions, periodicals, stationery; pure liquors for medical purposes
E. J. Owenhouse, Bozeman, Mont. — stock saddles, Concord harness, fancy bits and spurs, chaparejos, reatas, quirts, hackamores
Minneapolis & St. Louis R'y and the "Famous Albert Lea Route" (with map)
Brand: Medora Stage & F. Co., P.O. Medora — horse brand on left shoulder; horses strung on stage stations between Medora and Deadwood; $25 reward
Brand: E. W. Casey, Frank S. Moore, Manager, P.O. Medora — KC and F on left hip and shoulder; range O'Donnell creek
Brand: Sloping Bottom Ranch, Lloyd Roberts, Proprietor, P.O. Medora — brand on left hip; range Little Missouri 7 mi S of N. P. R. R.
Brand: Badger Cattle Company, Howard Eaton, Mgr., P.O. Medora — VI on left hip; range Beaver creek and Little Missouri river
Brand: Dorr Clark, Spearfish, Dakota — VVV on left side; range Belle Fourche
Brand: Clark & Plum, Spearfish, Dakota — E6 on left side; range Grand river
Brand: Little Missouri Horse Company, H. R. Tarbell, Mgr., Medora — brand on left shoulder; range Davis creek and Little Missouri river
Brand: W. N. Thompson & Co., Wm. Dantz, Manager, P.O. Medora — TD and quarter-circle diamond brands
Brand: LeMoyne Cattle Co. (Limited), D. K. Wade, Manager, Medora — LC brands
Brand: Soho Cattle Co., Chas. Eaton, Manager, Medora — SO on left side
Brand: Chimney Butte Ranch, Theodore Roosevelt, Proprietor, Ferris & Merrifield, Managers, P.O. Medora — range six miles south of N. P. R. R. on Little Missouri; Maltese-cross brand on left hip, or right side, both or either; down cut dewlap
Brand: Bullion Creek Horse Ranch, Jack Bullion, Prop., Medora — SS on left hip; range Bullion creek, twenty miles south of Medora
Brand: N. P. Refrigerator Car Co., Medora — JP and other brands on left side; also steers bought of Mason & Lovell; ranges Little Missouri river and Beaver creek
Brand: Spring Creek Ranch, L. D. & B. Rumsey, J. L. Truscott, Manager, P.O. Medora — circle-R on left hip and side; both ears swallow-forked; range south of N. P. R. R. on Little Missouri
Brand: Berry, Boice & Co., P.O. Keith, Montana — brand on right hip, side and shoulder; range south of N. P. R. R., Little Missouri and Beaver creek
Brand: E. G. Paddock, P.O. Medora — six-inch circle-dot on both sides; range six miles north of crossing of N. P. R. R. and Little Missouri; horse brand four-inch circle-dot
Brand: Lydia S. Fuller, Frank S. Moore, Manager, P.O. Medora — LSF on left shoulder; range O'Donnell creek
Brand: Custer Trail Cattle Co., F. Alden Eaton, Supt., P.O. Medora — HK in circle and other brands; range Little Missouri river, Deep and Davis creeks
Brand: Towers & Gudgell, P.O. Keith, Montana — OX and other brands
Brand: Bad Lands Cattle Co., M. Wadsworth, Manager, P.O. Medora — three brands; range Little Missouri fifteen miles north of Medora
Brand: Neimmela Ranch, Gregor Lang, Manager, P.O. Medora — thistle brand on left or right shoulder; range Keogh crossing of Little Missouri to Pretty butte
articles.summary: Directory of page 4 advertisements and cattle-brand notices.

events.date_basis: Brand ad in Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Chimney Butte Ranch brand advertised: Theodore Roosevelt, proprietor
events.summary: The Cow Boy carried the brand notice of the Chimney Butte Ranch, Theodore Roosevelt proprietor, with Ferris & Merrifield as managers, ranging six miles south of the railroad on the Little Missouri.
events.excerpt: Chimney Butte Ranch. Theodore Roosevelt, Proprietor. Ferris & Merrifield, Managers.

events.date_basis: "last Friday evening" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: Citizens' meeting organizes fire department, school board and order
events.summary: A citizens' meeting called to order by the Marquis de Morès and chaired by A. T. Packard elected fire chiefs for each side of the river, appointed a new school board and a cleanliness committee, and charged the fire committee with keeping order since there is no county organization.
events.excerpt: The meeting last Friday evening was called to order by Marquis de Mores and A. T. Packard was elected chairman.

events.date_basis: Announcement in Thu 14 May 1885 issue for June purchases
events.title: Marquis de Morès announces June cattle buying at Sully Creek corrals
events.summary: As president of the Northern Pacific Refrigerator Car Company, the Marquis de Morès offered Little Missouri cattlemen Chicago prices less seventy cents per hundred for beef and dry cows delivered during June at the Sully Creek corrals.
events.excerpt: will give them during June for the beef and dry cows that they wish to sell, Chicago prices less seventy cents per hundred

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Refrigerator Car Co. builds corrals and clears bottoms for slaughter-house supply
events.summary: The Refrigerator Car Co. built two stockade corrals holding about a thousand cattle each, with scales, on the bottom this side of the Custer Trail ranch, and was clearing the river bottoms above Pete Book's coal mine; Hashknife cattle are to come down Sully creek and Montana cattle down Garner creek.
events.excerpt: Two large corrals have been built on the bottom this side of the Custer Trail ranch.

events.date_basis: "last night" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: Dr. Heber Robarts retained as the Marquis's family and company physician
events.summary: Dr. Heber Robarts came up to see patients and has been retained by the Marquis de Morès as family and company physician; he will spend about three days a week in Medora beginning about June 1.
events.excerpt: He has been retained as family and company physician by the Marquis

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Judge and family visit the Marquis de Morès
events.summary: A judge (name damaged in the scan), his wife and two daughters were in Medora visiting the Marquis de Morès.
events.excerpt: Judge [illegible], wife and two daughters are here visiting the Marquis.

events.date_basis: "a week ago Tuesday" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: Frank Wadsworth accidentally shot
events.summary: Frank Wadsworth was accidentally shot; his leg was amputated the next day.
events.excerpt: he was accidentally shot last Tuesday and that his leg was amputated Wednesday

events.date_basis: "Friday at noon" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: Death of Frank Wadsworth
events.summary: Frank Wadsworth died Friday at noon of a gunshot wound; the bullet, never found, was believed to have entered his abdomen. The Cow Boy called him a quiet man widely mourned.
events.excerpt: came the sad news of his death, occuring Friday at noon. It is seldom that a death is so widely mourned

events.date_basis: "last Sunday" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: Frank Wadsworth buried at Belfield
events.summary: Funeral services for Frank Wadsworth were held at Belfield, conducted by Rev. H. B. Shaffner, with a number of Medora citizens attending; he was buried near the church.
events.excerpt: The funeral services took place at Belfield last Sunday, a number of citizens from here, attending.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Cow Boy warns after two fatal gun accidents
events.summary: Following two recent fatal accidental shootings, the Cow Boy called such accidents little short of criminal and urged care in handling guns.
events.excerpt: such accidents are little short of criminal

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Warning against shooting on the east side of the track
events.summary: The Cow Boy warned that any further shooting on its side of the track would be taken seriously.
events.excerpt: Any further shooting on this side of the track will mean business

events.date_basis: "last Saturday evening" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: George Bicknell wins mile race at the skating rink
events.summary: George Bicknell won the mile race at the rink; in a later scrub race Johnny Chute ran a mile (thirty-six laps) in six minutes.
events.excerpt: The mile race at the rink last Saturday evening, was won by George Bicknell.

events.date_basis: "next Saturday" after Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: Necktie and sun-bonnet prizes planned at the rink
events.summary: Prizes were to be given at the rink for the largest necktie worn by a gentleman and the prettiest sun-bonnet worn by a lady.
events.excerpt: a prize will be given to the gentleman wearing the largest necktie

events.date_basis: "Monday" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: Medora town-plat survey completed
events.summary: The survey of the town-plat was completed and Mr. Heinze returned to Bismarck; the previous survey was found to be six inches to four feet off.
events.excerpt: The survey of the town-plat is completed and Mr. Heinze returned to Bismarck, Monday.

events.date_basis: "Monday" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: Peter Book begins the season's brick-making
events.summary: Peter Book began making brick and planned to make over a million this summer, his 600,000 of last year having been used up.
events.excerpt: Peter Book commenced making brick Monday and will make over a million this summer.

events.date_basis: "yesterday" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: A. M. Sinnott leaves east for Massachusetts
events.summary: A. M. Sinnott went east on train No. 2 to Bismarck and on to Marshfield, Mass.
events.excerpt: A. M. Sinnott went east on No. 2, yesterday

events.date_basis: "Tuesday evening" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: Frank Keeler family arrives in Medora
events.summary: Mr. and Mrs. Frank Keeler and baby arrived and are boarding at the Pyramid Park hotel.
events.excerpt: Mr. & Mrs. Frank Keeler and baby arrived Tuesday evening

events.date_basis: "the first of the week" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: N. P. superintendent Green and roadmaster Ray visit Medora
events.summary: Superintendent Green and roadmaster Ray of the railroad were in Medora early in the week.
events.excerpt: Superintendent Green and road-master Ray were in Medora the first of the week.

events.date_basis: "Sunday" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: Stage superintendent Allen and Wm. Van Driesche leave for the Hills
events.summary: Superintendent Allen of the stage line went out on the coach for the Black Hills, possibly not to return; Wm. Van Driesche also left for the Hills on Sunday morning's coach.
events.excerpt: Superintendent Allen went out on the coach Sunday for the Hills.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Goodall and Ryder pull the stock off the stage road
events.summary: John Goodall and Mose Ryder were pulling all the stock off the stage road and were expected back in a few days.
events.excerpt: John Goodall and Mose Ryder are now pulling all the stock off the stage road

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Cow Boy answers the Deadwood Pioneer on the Medora–Black Hills railroad
events.summary: Replying to the Deadwood Pioneer, the Cow Boy said capitalists declined to build a railroad from Medora to the Hills because Hills merchants broke contracts to ship via the Northern Pacific, and that the stage line had been a feeler for the Hills trade.
events.excerpt: had half the Hills merchants stuck to their promises they would now have direct or convenient railroad connection with the N. P.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Sentinel Butte quarantine: 950 Arkansas cattle turned loose
events.summary: A trainload of 950 cattle belonging to F. W. Fry of Arkansas was quarantined for several days at Sentinel Butte, apparently under Montana's pleuro-pneumonia law, then turned loose there on railroad orders and widely scattered.
events.excerpt: A train load of cattle, nine hundred and fifty head, have been quarantined for several days at Sentinel Butte.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Eastern round-ups finish with few cattle found
events.summary: The two eastern round-ups north and south of the track finished their work, finding very few cattle though they went east of Gladstone.
events.excerpt: Very few cattle were found although the round-up went east of Gladstone.

events.date_basis: Round-up schedule dated May 25, 1885
events.title: Little Missouri round-up (District No. 6) to begin at mouth of Box Elder
events.summary: Round-up District No. 6, W. P. Osterhout foreman, was to begin at the mouth of Box Elder and work down the Little Missouri and up Big Beaver to the railroad; District No. 7, R. H. Moore foreman, was to begin the same day at the mouth of the Yellowstone.
events.excerpt: Beginning at the mouth of Box Elder, May 25, 1885; thence working down the Little Missouri

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Doc Day sells 3,000 steers to Berry, Boice & Co.
events.summary: Doc Day sold 3,000 head of one- and two-year-old steers from the Day & Edgar range south of Dodge to Berry, Boice & Co., for delivery on the railroad about mid-June and a drive to Montana (reprinted from the Globe Live Stock Journal).
events.excerpt: Doc Day has sold from the Day & Edgar range, south of Dodge, 3000 head of steers

events.date_basis: "first week in June" per Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Slaughter-house to open for the season
events.summary: Work at the slaughter-house was expected to open for the season the first week in June, with cattle contracted for delivery by then.
events.excerpt: Work at the slaughter-house will probably open for the season during the first week in June.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Improvements at the slaughter-house
events.summary: A boiler for drying blood was set up in the old slaughter-house, its cold-storage room was torn out for rebuilding, and a boiler-plate tank was sunk in the well below the quicksand.
events.excerpt: A boiler has been set in position in the old slaughter-house to be used in drying blood.

events.date_basis: "by June 1" per Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Arch. Boyd's hotel to open
events.summary: The hotel, with Arch. Boyd as proprietor, was to be finished, furnished and ready for business by June 1.
events.excerpt: The hotel will be all finished, furnished and ready for business by June 1.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Railroad right of way to be made a park; sage brush to be cleared
events.summary: Work was to begin turning the railroad right of way into a park, leaving a wide street with Company buildings facing the road, and the Company intended to clear sage brush from Medora's lots and streets.
events.excerpt: Work will soon begin on turning the railroad right of way into a park.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Medora cleans up and sets out shade trees
events.summary: Residents took up cleaning the town with a will, and a number of shade trees were being set out.
events.excerpt: now we think we can boast as clean a town as there is on the line of the road

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Side-tracks raised under Paul Moore
events.summary: The Medora side-tracks were raised to overcome the grade onto the main track, under the superintendence of Paul Moore.
events.excerpt: The side-tracks have all been raised to overcome the grade in getting on the main track.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: E. G. Paddock moves house across the river; Fred Banan to open barber shop
events.summary: E. G. Paddock bought Geo. Fitzgerald's old dwelling across the river and set it up next to his barn; Fred Banan will use it as a barber shop.
events.excerpt: Fred Banan will occupy it as a barber shop.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: New clothing store managed by T. W. Gordon
events.summary: A new branch clothing store managed by T. W. Gordon advertised at length and was expected to do a large business.
events.excerpt: the new clothing store managed by T. W. Gordon, is conducted on first-class principles

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Yack Wah opens a laundry
events.summary: Yack Wah announced a Chinese laundry at the Metropolitan hotel, by card in this issue.
events.excerpt: "Yack Wah start um [laundly?] by Fitzglib"

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Soap works and tannery expected; money-order office likely
events.summary: It was considered almost certain that soap works and a tannery would be built in Medora this summer, and Medora had a good prospect of becoming a money-order office.
events.excerpt: It is now almost certain that soap works and a tannery will be built here this summer.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: School committee struggles with school debts
events.summary: Last year's school committee had trouble collecting money for school debts, with townspeople objecting to bearing the whole burden while saloon license money went to Mandan.
events.excerpt: Last year's school committee is having a parrot and monkey time collecting money for school debts.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: T. Martin ill; weather report to run weekly
events.summary: T. Martin was sick for several days with Rassie Deffebach minding the drug store; his weather report will now be published weekly at the request of Mr. Rich of the Badger Cattle Co.
events.excerpt: Hereafter, Mr. Martin's weather report will be published weekly

events.date_basis: "For week ending May 13"
events.title: Dry, clear week; coldest May 7, warmest May 13
events.summary: T. Martin's record for the week ending May 13 showed 4½ clear and 2½ fair days, no snow, northwest winds, a low of 24 degrees at 6 a.m. May 7 and a high of 84 at 6 p.m. May 13.
events.excerpt: Coldest day.....May 7. | Warmest day..May 13.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Mrs. Draper operated on for a tumor
events.summary: Mrs. Draper remained very ill after an operation to remove a tumor performed by Drs. Robarts and McIntosh.
events.excerpt: the operation for the removal of a tumor, performed by Drs. Robarts and McIntosh

events.date_basis: "Saturday" before Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: Mrs. Porter returns from Chicago
events.summary: Mrs. Porter returned from Chicago.
events.excerpt: Mrs. Porter returned from Chicago Saturday

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Miss Mead of Bismarck brings millinery
events.summary: Miss Mead of Bismarck was in Medora with a line of millinery goods.
events.excerpt: Miss Mead of Bismarck, is here with a line of millinery goods.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: McKenzie & O'Brien to move blacksmith shop
events.summary: McKenzie & O'Brien were to move their blacksmith shop to the Cow Boy's side of the track in a day or two.
events.excerpt: McKenzie & O'Brien will move their blacksmith shop to this side of the track

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Chas. Cook puts up an awning
events.summary: Chas. Cook put up an awning in front of his store.
events.excerpt: Chas. Cook has put up a much-needed awning in front of his store

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Railroad men say Medora leads in stop-offs
events.summary: Railroad men said more people stopped off at Medora than at any other town between Mandan and Miles City.
events.excerpt: more people stop off at Medora than at any other town between Mandan and Miles City

events.date_basis: "next week" after Thu 14 May 1885
events.title: J. S. Warn and F. D. Foster expected back
events.summary: A telegram from J. S. Warn said he would be home next week, and F. D. Foster was expected back next week with his family.
events.excerpt: he will be home next week "dead or alive,"

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: John Munro cultivating the butte farm
events.summary: John Munro was cultivating the butte farm.
events.excerpt: John Munro is cultivating the butte farm.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 14 May 1885 issue
events.title: Glee club proposed
events.summary: A glee club was described as one of the near probabilities in Medora.
events.excerpt: A glee club is one of the near probabilities.
